name: Broadsheet / editorial columns
structure: grid-template-columns: repeat(12, 1fr); body copy locked to a 6-8 column measure (60-75ch), never full width; images break the column with grid-column: span 12 only as relief; masthead = rule line + wordmark, no hero image required
first_viewport: Masthead, then the first story starts immediately; a deck (subhead) under the headline carries the pitch
primary_action: Inline in the copy or a small rule-bounded button, never a giant CTA block
density: medium-high; whitespace is a column, not a padding value
memorable: Feels authored and trustworthy for long-form
failure_mode: Becomes a Word document if type hierarchy (weight, not just size) does not carry the structure
mobile_fallback: Single column at the same measure; column rules become horizontal hairlines between stories

name: Poster (one giant object)
structure: One dominant element occupies 70-100vh, often object-fit: cover bleeding off all edges; everything else is caption-scaled; no header chrome competing
first_viewport: The object IS the viewport; one caption-scale line of copy anchored to a corner or the baseline
primary_action: A single word-sized link/button anchored to one corner or the baseline of the object, never dead center
scroll: None, or a hard cut to a completely different second screen
failure_mode: Nothing to do if the object is not good enough to carry it alone
mobile_fallback: Object crops to portrait focal point; caption and action stack at the bottom edge

name: Poster stack (sequence of full-viewport screens)
structure: scroll-snap-type: y mandatory; each section is 100svh with its own single dominant object and one line; hard cuts between screens, no shared header
first_viewport: Screen one is a poster; a small index (dots or numbers) shows how many screens follow
primary_action: On the final screen only, at poster scale
scroll: Snaps screen to screen; each screen is complete on its own
memorable: Cinematic pacing; each screen one idea
failure_mode: Scroll-jacking fatigue if more than 5-6 screens or if snapping fights the user
mobile_fallback: Native fit: each screen is a phone screen; keep 100svh not 100vh

name: Split-screen (50/50 or 70/30)
structure: display: grid; grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr (or 7fr 3fr); one half position: sticky while the other scrolls, or both independently scrollable
first_viewport: Two ideas at once: text one side, product/proof the other; the seam is a deliberate edge (rule, colour change), not a gap
primary_action: In the lighter, usually fixed, half
scroll: One side pins while the other scrolls past it
memorable: Forces a comparison or duality the visitor resolves
failure_mode: Coin-flip layout if there is no real duality to represent
mobile_fallback: Stack: the fixed half becomes a sticky top band (max 40svh), the scrolling half follows

name: Asymmetric offset grid
structure: 12-column grid; elements span uneven, non-mirrored ranges (grid-column: 1/8 and 6/13 overlapping) with intentional bleed; a shared baseline grid underneath keeps overlaps disciplined
first_viewport: One element breaks the frame (image overlaps the text block) to establish this is not a template
primary_action: Off the optical centre, lower-left or upper-right
scroll: Elements re-offset per section; never the same offset twice in a row
memorable: Feels art-directed, not assembled from a component library
failure_mode: Reads as broken if overlaps do not respect the underlying baseline grid
mobile_fallback: Offsets shrink to 1-2 column shifts; overlaps become slight negative margins; never full stacking to centred

name: Bento (modular tile grid)
structure: CSS grid with explicit grid-template-areas and UNEVEN spans (one 2x2 lead tile + 1x1 + 1x2), consistent gutter; the lead tile must be at least 3x the area of the smallest
first_viewport: One large tile establishes the category; smaller tiles are supporting facts, not equal siblings
primary_action: Inside the largest tile, not a separate section
scroll: The grid may be a single screen or repeat per section
failure_mode: Devolves into equal-size cards the moment span variance is dropped, becoming the template it was meant to escape
mobile_fallback: Lead tile full width first, then a 2-column masonry of the rest; never a single column of equal cards

name: Dense operate / console
structure: Shell is height: 100vh; overflow: hidden; multi-pane with hard-pixel gutters (not rem-padded cards); monospace or tabular-figure numerals; a status bar or command line on top
first_viewport: No hero: the tool is the first screen
primary_action: Keyboard-first: command palette or inline action, rarely a big button
scroll: Panes scroll independently; the outer shell never scrolls
memorable: Feels like an instrument, not a website
failure_mode: Noise, unless density is paired with real hierarchy (contrast, grouping)
mobile_fallback: Not a squeeze: one pane at a time with a bottom pane-switcher; status bar stays

name: Index / list-first
structure: No card grid at all: one vertical list, each row a flex line with 2-4 columns (date, title, tag, arrow); hairline or whitespace separation
first_viewport: The list starts above the fold; at most a one-line intro
primary_action: The row IS the action: the whole row is the click target
scroll: Long, uninterrupted list scroll, virtualised if needed
density: low visual density, high information density
memorable: Radically calm; respects the scanning eye
failure_mode: Feels empty if rows carry no supporting metadata
mobile_fallback: Rows wrap to two lines: title first, metadata second in a smaller size

name: Scroll narrative (pinned steps)
structure: Sections pinned via position: sticky while inner content is driven by scroll progress (scroll-linked transforms, counters, diagram assembly); no navigation visible until the story resolves
first_viewport: An establishing shot or a question; no nav
primary_action: Only after the story resolves, at the end
scroll: Scroll position drives state changes; content changes, not just opacity
density: low per screen, long total page
failure_mode: Nausea or sluggishness if scroll-jacking fights the user; needs a static in-order fallback for reduced motion
mobile_fallback: Same pinned steps but shorter; every revealed state must also exist as static, in-order content

name: Magazine feature with pull-quotes
structure: Column grid; pull-quote blocks set in a different size/family break grid-column across the gutter every 3-4 screens; headline + deck + byline metadata
first_viewport: Large headline, deck, byline; the first paragraph begins on screen
memorable: Long copy stays readable and varied without cards
failure_mode: Pull-quotes read as filler unless they add a second voice
mobile_fallback: Single column; pull-quotes go full-bleed with a rule above and below

name: Catalog / product sheet
structure: A repeating unit (image + fixed-position spec table beside it) repeats identically down the page; category header + filter/sort bar instead of a hero
first_viewport: Header, filter bar, then the first two units
primary_action: Inside the repeating unit (Add/Select), never once globally
scroll: Regular, predictable rhythm; scanability is the point
memorable: Trustworthy because every entry is comparable
failure_mode: Boring without a strong photographic or data-typography system
mobile_fallback: Unit stacks image over table; filter bar becomes a sticky chip row

name: Spec-sheet / datasheet
structure: Tabular grid with hairline rules (border: 1px solid), monospace or tabular figures right-aligned with decimal alignment, labelled diagrams inset into the table, a title block in a corner
first_viewport: A technical drawing or diagram, not a photo; the key table starts immediately
primary_action: None, or a minimal download link
scroll: Rarely far; often one dense screen
memorable: Reads as engineering truth, zero gloss
failure_mode: Illegible without real tabular typography (aligned decimals, consistent units column)
mobile_fallback: Table becomes a two-column definition list; diagram goes full width above it

name: Zine collage
structure: Layered absolutely-positioned elements, rotated text, torn/taped edges, overlapping z-index; a hidden grid underneath anchors the chaos
first_viewport: Texture before message: chaos on purpose, one legible entry point
primary_action: A hand-drawn-feeling button or a circled/underlined word
scroll: Sections interrupt each other; no consistent rhythm
failure_mode: Unusable and inaccessible if the chaos is not secretly anchored to a grid; contrast must still pass
mobile_fallback: Rotations drop to ±2°, layers become a single column with overlaps as negative margins

name: Map / spatial
structure: Canvas/SVG 2D space (pan + zoom) instead of vertical document flow; content are pins or nodes; a legend is a first-class fixed element
first_viewport: A zoomed-out overview of the whole space with the legend pinned
primary_action: Clicking a node opens detail; no page-level CTA
failure_mode: Disorienting on small screens without a forced linear fallback
mobile_fallback: A list of nodes ordered by region/proximity with the legend as a filter row; the map is an optional secondary view

name: Timeline / ledger
structure: A single vertical spine (a rule with real visual weight) with entries branching to one side; chronological order enforced by DOM order; entries carry date, amount or status in aligned columns
first_viewport: The most recent or first entry with a clear start marker
scroll: Continuous along the spine; entries reveal as they cross the viewport
failure_mode: A bullet list if the spine has no visual weight
mobile_fallback: Spine moves to the left edge; entries take the full remaining width

name: Single-column reading
structure: One column, max-width: 65ch, centred, line-height 1.6-1.8; no visual events
first_viewport: Title and the first paragraph, nothing else
primary_action: At the end of the text, or none
memorable: Maximum trust and focus; the content is the only argument
failure_mode: Deadly for anything that needs demonstration rather than explanation
mobile_fallback: Native fit; measure holds via ch units

name: Sidebar-first tool
structure: grid-template-columns: 240px 1fr; a persistent rail (left or right) across all states; main area swaps content; no top nav, no hero
first_viewport: The rail is the nav; the main pane shows the primary object, not a welcome screen
primary_action: Inline in the main pane per context
scroll: Main pane scrolls; rail stays pinned
density: high in the rail, variable in the pane
memorable: Establishes this is software, not a page about software
failure_mode: Generic the instant the rail is the same icon-plus-label list as every admin template
mobile_fallback: Rail collapses to a bottom bar (≤5 items) or a sheet; never a hamburger with the same list

name: Card-less operate UI
structure: Real HTML tables and definition lists instead of div cards; separation from table rules, not box-shadow; sticky header row; row-level actions
first_viewport: A toolbar/filter row, then data starts immediately
scroll: Table scrolls internally with a sticky header
memorable: A serious tool built by people who use it
failure_mode: The cards-as-default habit is so strong this needs an explicit rule to hold
mobile_fallback: Rows become two-line list items with the 2-3 most important columns; the rest behind a row expand
